notes.title: Global supports give convexity on the finite feasible domain
notes.plain: The same EReal loss f, convex feasible set V and canonical ordered divergence Bψ(a;b)=ψ(a)−ψ(b)−Dψ(b)[a−b] are used throughout. Properness excludes negative infinity everywhere and supplies one finite point. At every feasible z, a source subgradient supports f at every ambient y. This global support condition implies that f is finite at every point of V; outside V, positive infinity is allowed. The first bridge uses an arbitrary real inner-product space. The other two explicitly retain completeness from the reused minimum-order API. Finite Euclidean source spaces are covered; minimal assumptions are not claimed. The result is convexity of z ↦ (f z).toReal restricted to V. Taking toReal at infinity gives zero, so the total real function need not be globally convex. The proof selects a global support at the feasible convex combination, compares the two feasible endpoints, and cancels the weighted inner products after feasible finiteness has been established.
notes.intuition: Evaluate a support at the convex combination and compare both feasible endpoints.
notes.why: Preserve extended losses in the required Chapter 2 general prescient dependency.

notes.title: The actual extended proximal minimum has a real finite-part equivalent
notes.plain: The same EReal loss f, convex feasible set V and canonical ordered divergence Bψ(a;b)=ψ(a)−ψ(b)−Dψ(b)[a−b] are used throughout. Properness excludes negative infinity everywhere and supplies one finite point. At every feasible z, a source subgradient supports f at every ambient y. This global support condition implies that f is finite at every point of V; outside V, positive infinity is allowed. The first bridge uses an arbitrary real inner-product space. The other two explicitly retain completeness from the reused minimum-order API. Finite Euclidean source spaces are covered; minimal assumptions are not claimed. For a supplied p in V and finite f on V, the actual EReal objective f(z)+η⁻¹ Bψ(z;x) has a minimum at p exactly when its real finite-part objective does. This order equivalence permits every real η, including zero and negative values, with Lean’s total inverse. It needs no convexity, derivative, positive step size or attainment premise beyond the supplied minimum in each direction. The center x may be outside V and the loss domain. The proof reuses the shared minOn_finitePart_iff on the actual penalized objective.

notes.title: An extended proximal minimum gives the signed one-step comparison
notes.plain: The same EReal loss f, convex feasible set V and canonical ordered divergence Bψ(a;b)=ψ(a)−ψ(b)−Dψ(b)[a−b] are used throughout. Properness excludes negative infinity everywhere and supplies one finite point. At every feasible z, a source subgradient supports f at every ambient y. This global support condition implies that f is finite at every point of V; outside V, positive infinity is allowed. The first bridge uses an arbitrary real inner-product space. The other two explicitly retain completeness from the reused minimum-order API. Finite Euclidean source spaces are covered; minimal assumptions are not claimed. For the one-step comparison, η is positive, V is convex, f is proper and has global supports at every feasible point, p belongs to V and actually minimizes the EReal penalized objective there. The generator ψ has actual ambient derivatives at both x and p. Every u in the same V satisfies η((f p).toReal−(f u).toReal) ≤ Bψ(u;x)−Bψ(u;p)−Bψ(p;x). Both negative residuals and their target/base order are retained. No infinity subtraction, loss derivative, convexity of ψ, closedness of V, bounded domain or existence of minimizers is asserted. Dropping residuals requires separate nonnegativity hypotheses.

legacy_reader_wording_corrections.before: One canonical total real function Dψ(a,b)=ψ(a)-ψ(b)-Dψ(b)[a-b], using the actual Frechet derivative fderiv of ψ. The second argument is the base. At a nondifferentiable base fderiv defaults to zero; this total algebraic formula alone is not a source differentiability, positivity, metric or separation theorem. The core uses any real normed vector space; only the gradient conversion needs a complete real inner-product space. The source is finite Euclidean, ψ:X->R strictly convex/differentiable on intX; source-domain and ambient-extension locality are not silently identified. The supplied p belongs to V and actually minimizes f(z)+ηinverse Dψ(z,x) there; f is real convex on the same V, η>0, and ψ is ambient differentiable at BOTH x and p. x may be outside V. No loss derivative, ψ convexity/strictness, closedness, coercivity or existence theorem is required by this real helper. It concludes the comparison for every u in V with both negative residuals retained. Nonnegative residual values require separate convexity hypotheses; they cannot be discarded from this theorem alone. Differentiate only h(z)=ηinverse Dψ(z,x) at the selected minimum p. Its derivative is ηinverse(Dψ(p)-Dψ(x)). The accepted real nonsmooth convex-minimizer comparison gives f(p)-f(u)<=ηinverse(Dψ(p)-Dψ(x))[u-p]. Multiply by positive η and use the three-point identity with (p,x,u), obtaining Dψ(u,x)-Dψ(u,p)-Dψ(p,x). The previous-base derivative hypothesis is retained for source validity even though the fixed dual map is already linear in this proof. This is an actual-minimum comparison, not an assumed regret/stability bound or a sequence construction. The ordered nonquadratic divergences are9/64 and11/64. Each universal comparison and separately selected final numerical proof branch retains actual public proximal_one_step VALUE; final bounds -1/2<=-5/16 and -1/2<=1/2 use equality transport of that comparison. Divergence formulas also use actual public gradient conversion. Nonnegative has a full generic public VALUE witness, with no claimed concrete Test VALUE use.
